headline: High risk: Plandex’s writable shell/network defaults can conflict with Caveman’s MCP-enabled content workflows, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Caveman has use_mcp=true and exposes files like CLAUDE.md, while Plandex reads/writes a project directory and can run shell steps. That creates a plausible bridge where Caveman-authored content can reach Plandex as trusted input. The pair lacks explicit provenance controls in the profiles, so injection risk is real but not proven high.
conditions: IF Caveman content is copied into Plandex plans or prompts via shared files or MCP
IF Plandex parses project files or shell output as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of shared files into prompts
Require manual review of any Caveman-generated text before Plandex uses it
Separate Caveman and Plandex workspaces
Add a provenance banner to imported content
requires-engineering: enforce instruction/data separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Plandex has broad network egress and reads/writes the project directory. If those files contain secrets or sensitive notes, Plandex can transmit them to a model provider or cloud backend. Caveman’s own network_egress is none, but the pair still leaks through Plandex.
conditions: IF sensitive notes or memory files are placed in the shared project directory
IF Plandex sends file contents to its model provider or Plandex Cloud
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use a redacted copy of notes for Plandex
Turn off auto-upload or cloud sync if available
Review files before adding them to Plandex plans
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before outbound calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Caveman supports multiple instances and uses MCP, but its filesystem write scope is not documented. The pair therefore has overlapping mutable workspace pressure, and uncertainty about Caveman’s write behavior pushes severity upward. Concurrent edits can corrupt files or git state in default collaborative use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or project directory
IF Plandex auto-applies changes while Caveman also edits shared files
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Serialize edits with a human gate
Commit frequently to isolate conflicts
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex is a coding tool with review-then-apply and optional auto-apply, so it can act on upstream text. Caveman produces content-writing outputs and project notes that Plandex may consume. That makes A-to-B propagation plausible, but Plandex’s review step reduces the chance of blind execution, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Caveman-generated notes are imported into Plandex plans
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled or review is skipped
mitigations: Require a second human review before apply
Keep Caveman outputs as drafts only
Disable auto-apply
Ask Plandex to cite source lines before acting
requires-engineering: add verification checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only open-source tools, and no regulated data class or residency mismatch is documented. Caveman touches session logs and memory files, while Plandex handles source code and model-provider keys, but the profiles do not show a concrete compliance breach pathway. The other agent is not cited beyond the pair context because no specific cross-border or regulated-data flow is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is manually placed into either tool
IF deployment policy requires retention or residency controls not configured here
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either tool
Review retention settings before use
Store secrets outside project files
Document data-handling boundaries for operators
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
